That was a bug and is fixed in the GitHub version:

https://github.com/jniedballa/camtrapR/commit/677d389cab65906eff1a39486c18c77cba08c0b3

Beat regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] recordTable format does not match camOp matrix
messages.subject_clean: [camtrapR] recordTable format does not match camOp matrix
messages.body_plain:
Hello Nadia,
You can use a manually created record table. All you need is the station, species and date/time column.

Run
data(recordTableSampleMultiSeason)
for an example.

And yes, the names of the stations must match exactly row names in the camera operation matrix.

To get a better idea if the workflow follow the examples in th vignette (not exactly you scenario but close enough) and examine the objects involved.

Also, in general it helps if you show the code and the error messges you got. Then I can answer more specifically.

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Re: recordTable function using data sheet generated from Timelapse software
messages.subject_clean: [camtrapR] Re: recordTable function using data sheet generated from Timelapse software
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
The tables from Timelapse can be used directly, so they already are record tables and there is no need to convert anything. filterRecordTable is an optional step.

One can also proceed with detectionHistory (if occupancy analyses are the aim).
In that case one needs to adjust speciesCol, stationCol and dateTimeCol, and possibly adjust dateTimeFormat.

Best regards,
Jürgen

On Thu, Oct 19, 2023, 23:24 Nor Bazilah Razali <norbazil...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi Nadia,
>
> Recently, I figured out how to extract data from the Timelapse datasheet using filterRecordTable (Filter species record table for temporal independence). First, you need to install these packages to enable the filterRecordTable function:
>
> install.packages("remotes") # if not installed
> install.packages("R.rsp")   # if not installed
> remotes::install_github("jniedballa/camtrapR", build_vignettes = TRUE)
>
> Then,  you make the timelapse datasheet from csv format to data frame using data.frame function. Afterward, you tally the speciesCol, stationCol, and recordDateTimeCol according to  Timelapse Datasheet. Mine might be different than yours.
>
> Below are the scripts I manage to make R run the filterRecordTable.
>
> timelapse <- read.csv("BRCT33.csv")
> dftimelapse <- data.frame(timelapse)
>
> rec_table_filt <- filterRecordTable(recordTable         = dftimelapse,
>                                     speciesCol          = "Species",
>                                     stationCol = "CamtrapID",
>                                     recordDateTimeCol   = "DateTime",
>                                     minDeltaTime        = 60,
>                                     deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastIndependentRecord")
>
> table(rec_table_filt$Species)
>
> Hope it helps.
>
> Best Regards,
> Bazilah

messages.subject_clean: Covariate beta.ranef.cont.ele not found in posterior matrix
messages.body_plain:
Hi camtrapR users and Jurgen,

I am facing a strange issue when trying to plot the results of this model.

mod.jags <- communityModel(data_list,
model="Occupancy",
occuCovs = list(ranef = c("ele","area","type")),
detCovsObservation = list(ranef=c("ndays","ndays_squared")),
intercepts = list(det = "ranef", occu = "ranef"),
speciesSiteRandomEffect = list(det = TRUE),
effortCov="effort",
richnessCategories="type",
modelFile="/beegfs/home/sanile/modelfile1.txt",
augmentation = c(maxknown = 60),
keyword_quadratic ="_squared")

summary(mod.jags)
# commOccu object for community occupancy model (in JAGS)
#
# 60 species,  79 stations,  3187 occasions
# 45551 occasions with effort
# Number of detections (by species): 0 - 222
#
# Available site covariates:
#  area, ele, type
#
# Used site covariates:
#  area, ele, type
#
# Available site-occasion covariates:
#  effort, ndays, ndays_squared

The values for  beta.ranef.cont.ele are properly reported when I explore the results  (attached as screenshot) using

fit.summary<-summary(out)
DT::datatable(round(fit.summary$statistics, 3))

but when I try to plot the results with

plot_effects(object = mod.jags, mcmc.list = out)$type

I got this warning message:
Error: Covariate beta.ranef.cont.ele not found in posterior matrix

Any suggestion is very much appreciated.

Stef

Hi all,

I have been able to understand my mistake. The model file was not exactly as the one used when the model was fit on a cluster computer.
Once I have recreated the exact model file, everything is fine.

I hope this can help someone else when sending the analysis to some powerful cluster computer.

Stef
